submission.justification: Absorber-F1 with 5 mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.174% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This represents an 18% improvement over the best Absorber-F3 configuration (3.827% at 6 mm) and a 38% improvement over the best Absorber-F2 configuration (5.144% at 4 mm). The simulation survey across the allowed thickness range (2-10 mm) shows that 5 mm is optimal for F1, with resolution degrading at both thinner and thicker plates. All three candidate materials are compatible with the mechanical support design and can be machined to required tolerances. While the hands-on maintenance constraint is noted, none of the project documents explicitly exclude any candidate material on radiation safety grounds, and all three remain listed as viable candidates. The 5 mm thickness also matches the reference simulation from 2025, providing consistency with earlier studies.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5 mm achieves 3.174% resolution, which is the best among all 24 configurations tested (3 materials × 8 thicknesses each)

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as a candidate material
Recommended thickness of 5 mm falls within the specified range of 2-10 mm

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: No explicit information about radioactivation or hands-on maintenance compatibility is provided in the project documents for any of the three candidate materials. All three remain listed as viable candidates without exclusions.
